text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of fluctuating extraocular muscle weakness (double vision), bulbar symptoms (implied by the need to rule out drooping/swallowing), and proximal limb weakness (difficulty climbing stairs) is classic for this autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder. I recommend requesting antibodies for Acetylcholine Receptor and MuSK, as well as a Chest CT to check for a thymoma.
